title: Living with a Changing Climate Across the Pacific
text:
01
      Pacific territorial CO₂ in the 2023 world total
      The first bar preserves the world scale. The second enlarges its first 0.1% so the covered Pacific share can be seen.
    
    
    
      A like-for-like comparison
      Both figures count territorial CO₂ in 2023 using the same Our World in Data release. They do not cover consumption-based emissions, emissions from land-use change or greenhouse gases other than CO₂. Five Pacific places in the project list had no 2023 value and are not included in the regional total.
    
  

  
    
      02
      Reported human and economic effects of four cyclones
      Event assessments report 65,000 people displaced by Cyclone Pam, 540,400 affected by Winston, about 80,000 affected by Gita and about 130,000 affected by Harold. Each assessment put the reported economic effects or losses above one-fifth of annual GDP; Pam’s assessment reached 64.1%.
    
    
    
      Different reports use different measures
      Affected people, displacement, damage and wider economic effects are not the same measure. The figures describe individual events and should not be added together or treated as a time series.
    
  

  
    
      03
      South Pacific cyclone tracks from 1980 to 2023
      IBTrACS records 508 storm tracks across the South Pacific from 1980 to 2023. Of these, 103 reached Category 3 or above in the archive’s USA intensity field. The map places the four event assessments within the wider regional record, but it does not test whether cyclone frequency or intensity changed over time.
    
    
      
        
        
      
      
        
          All tracks
          The archive contains 508 South Pacific storm tracks
          The archive begins well before the period shown here. The 1980 start keeps the view inside the modern satellite era.
        
        
          Recorded intensity
          The archive classifies 103 tracks as Category 3 or above
          The categories use the IBTrACS USA Saffir Simpson field. Agency wind standards differ, so this is an orientation layer rather than a trend test.
        
        
          Event assessments
          The highlighted tracks are Pam, Winston, Gita and Harold
          These are the four tracks linked to the event reports shown immediately before the map.
        
      
    
  

  
    
      04
      Sea-surface temperatures were higher in the recent decade
      Across all 21 places with complete data, the sea surface was warmer on average from 2014 to 2023 than from 1993 to 2002. The increase ranged from 0.21°C in French Polynesia to 0.49°C in Nauru. The rows below keep each place separate rather than replacing them with a single Pacific average.
    
    
    
      A change in average conditions
      The comparison shows the direction and size of the temperature shift. It does not measure how the change affected particular communities or ecosystems.
    
  

  
    
      05
      Annual coral heat stress at eight Pacific virtual stations
      Degree Heating Weeks combine how far temperatures rise above the local bleaching threshold with how long the heat persists. Annual maximum values reached or exceeded 4°C-weeks in multiple years and locations, while the timing and size of the peaks differed among stations.
    
    
    
      An accumulated heat-stress measure
      At 4°C-weeks, significant coral bleaching can occur; at 8°C-weeks, severe bleaching and coral mortality become likely. Degree Heating Weeks indicate heat stress, while observations at the reef are still needed to confirm whether bleaching occurred.
    
  

  
    
      06
      The sea level record moves into higher bands
      In 2023, all 21 records reported a positive anomaly: 20 were reported at +0.1 metre and Vanuatu at +0.2 metre. Higher bands became more common across the 1993-2023 period, although the source values are rounded to the nearest 0.1 metre.
    
    
    
      A broad regional measure
      The rounding makes transitions look abrupt and hides smaller changes. Local shorelines also respond to waves, storms, sediment and vertical land movement, so these records should not be read as local flood levels.
    
  

  
    
      07
      Annual rainfall and crop-yield changes across 15 Pacific places
      Across 450 paired country-years, the Pearson correlation between annual rainfall anomalies and year-to-year changes in reported crop yield was 0.04. Wetter years included both yield gains and losses, and the same was true in drier years.
    
    
    
      What the weak correlation means
      National annual values remove the timing and location of rainfall, while crop yields also vary with conditions that are not represented on this chart. The result does not show that rainfall is unimportant; it shows that one national rainfall anomaly is not enough to explain annual yield changes.
    
  

  
    
      08
      Renewable electricity generation across 18 Pacific places in 2023
      In 2023, renewables supplied 94.4% of recorded electricity in Tokelau and 52.1% in Fiji. They were the only two of 18 places where renewables passed the halfway mark. The chart covers electricity generation rather than transport fuels and other energy uses, which are tracked separately
    
    
    
      Reading the 2023 response
      The chart does not show how quickly each electricity system is changing. It shows the renewable share recorded in 2023 and the different starting points for further change.
    
  

  
    
      Sources
      Open data used in this story
      
        Our World in Data CO₂ datasetTerritorial CO₂ totals for the Pacific comparison and the world, 2023
        Pacific climate indicatorsSea-surface temperature, sea-level, annual rainfall anomaly and crop-yield records
        NOAA IBTrACS version 4.01South Pacific cyclone positions and recorded intensity, 1980-2023
        NOAA Coral Reef WatchAnnual maximum Degree Heating Weeks at eight virtual stations, 1985-2025
        Pacific power generationRenewable and non-renewable electricity generation, 2023
        Cyclone event assessmentsPamWinstonGitaHaroldEvent-specific people, displacement, economic-effect and GDP figures
      
      The reproducible tidyverse data build is in r/build_story.R. Derived tables are stored in the story folder. Sources were accessed on 9 August 2026. Event figures retain the definitions used by each assessment; the essay makes no event-attribution claim and calculates no combined climate-risk score.
      Built with love and curiosity using R and Quarto by Edo Danilyan.
